title: Search economy benchmark: subconscious agentic search versus graphify token cost
summary: Benchmark under bench/search-economy/ comparing three context assembly arms on identical code navigation queries: naive (grep plus read), subconscious agentic search (runAgenticContextSearches over a KB built by onboarding the target repo source), and graphify (AST subgraph via graphify query with a token budget). Two phases. Phase 1 retrieval first runs now in pure Node and measures context tokens emitted plus recall and precision against ground truth relevant symbols over the zonoid repo, yielding tokens per correct symbol. Phase 2 end to end is scaffolded but run deferred: a custom Terminal-Bench AbstractInstalledAgent adapter per arm measuring resolved rate plus total tokens from the jobs trajectories. Key asymmetry the design controls for: the subconscious arm indexes the KB task graph while graphify indexes source code structure, so the fair unit is the SAME code navigation task solved by three different context mechanisms, reported as a two by two capability matrix not a single winner. Graphify and Terminal-Bench both require Python (graphify is the pip package graphifyy, Terminal-Bench needs uv plus Docker) which is NOT installed on the current Windows box, so both the graphify arm and the Terminal-Bench e2e arm are scaffolded with their run deferred; only the Node retrieval bench runs now. Context: the existing bench/heldout harness already shows the on-search arm beats off on KB fact tasks (0 of 45 versus 7 of 8 edge solves) at higher token and latency cost, but those tasks are KB fact biased and unfair to graphify, which is why this new bench adds a code structure task family.
